source_text: Per unum hominem peccatum intravit in mundum et per peccatum mors, et ita in omnes homines pertransiit: mortem, non peccatum, in omnes transisse intellegunt
pass_a_gloss: Through one man sin entered into the world and through sin death, and so it passed through unto all human beings: they understand death, not sin, to have passed unto all

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Augustine reports that in the apostle’s words, “Through one man sin entered the world, and through sin death, and so it passed to all human beings,” the authors understand death, rather than sin, as what passed to everyone (Romans 5:12).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian and fellow bishops (Collective letter to Thessalonica, words preserved in Augustine, Contra duas epistolas Pelagianorum 2–4); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
